question: What is the primary physiological defect in diabetes mellitus?
explanation: Diabetes mellitus is characterized primarily by chronic high blood sugar levels resulting from problems with insulin. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h1)

question: The main function of insulin in the human body is to...

options.A: allow body cells to absorb glucose
options.B: stimulate the liver to produce more sugar
options.D: prevent the kidneys from filtering water

explanation: Insulin acts as a key that unlocks body cells so glucose from the bloodstream can enter and be used for energy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h1)

question: Cellular insulin resistance means that target tissues...

options.B: fail to respond properly to insulin
options.D: absorb too much sugar too fast

explanation: Insulin resistance occurs when cells do not respond effectively to the hormone, preventing normal glucose uptake. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which organ is responsible for producing the hormone insulin?
explanation: Specialized beta cells within the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas synthesize and secrete insulin. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h2)

question: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is fundamentally caused by...
explanation: Type 1 diabetes involves an immune-mediated destruction of the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h3)

question: Gestational diabetes mellitus is defined as glucose intolerance that begins...
explanation: Gestational diabetes specifically refers to high blood sugar that is first detected during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h3)

question: Urbanization contributes to rising diabetes rates in Nigeria primarily through...

options.B: shifts toward processed diets and physical inactivity
options.C: reduced access to traditional medical herbs
options.D: genetic mutations caused by factory pollution

explanation: Urban lifestyle changes often involve eating more calorie-dense foods and moving less, which triggers metabolic disease. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which factor is NOT a typical lifestyle risk factor for Type 2 diabetes?
explanation: Regular physical exercise protects against diabetes rather than acting as a risk factor. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the medical term for excessive thirst experienced by diabetic patients?
explanation: Polydipsia refers to the excessive thirst caused by fluid loss from high blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h5)

question: A fasting plasma glucose test result of 7.0 mmol/L or higher indicates...
explanation: A fasting plasma glucose level at or above 7.0 mmol/L meets the diagnostic threshold for diabetes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient taking insulin reports feeling shaky, sweaty, and dizzy. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Withhold all oral fluids and prepare for immediate surgery
options.B: Instruct the patient to exercise vigorously to burn off sugar
options.C: Check the blood glucose level and provide fast-acting carbohydrates
options.D: Administer a scheduled dose of long-acting insulin

explanation: Shakiness and sweating indicate hypoglycemia, which requires immediate confirmation and treatment with fast-acting sugar. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is rotating subcutaneous insulin injection sites clinically important?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling any needle pain
options.B: To stimulate local muscle growth in the limbs
options.C: To prevent lipodystrophy and ensure consistent drug absorption
options.D: To speed up the renal clearance of the medication

explanation: Rotating sites prevents abnormal fat buildup under the skin, which can erraticize how insulin is absorbed. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h6)

question: The primary goal of community-based diabetes screening programs is to...

options.A: provide free lifetime medication to all citizens
options.B: diagnose rare genetic disorders in newborns
options.C: detect hyperglycemia early before complications develop
options.D: eliminate the need for hospital-based doctors

explanation: Screening campaigns catch elevated blood sugar early, allowing for timely intervention and reduced complication risks. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which strategy is most effective for primary prevention of Type 2 diabetes in communities?

options.A: Promoting healthy diet and regular physical exercise
options.B: Distributing emergency insulin kits to every household
options.C: Isolating diagnosed patients from the general public
options.D: Mandating daily blood tests for all school children

explanation: Lifestyle modifications focusing on diet and exercise successfully prevent or delay the onset of Type 2 diabetes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h7)

question: Diabetic retinopathy is a chronic microvascular complication that specifically damages the...

options.A: peripheral nerves of the lower limbs
options.B: large coronary arteries of the heart
options.C: blood vessels in the retina of the eye

explanation: Retinopathy involves damage to the small blood vessels supplying the retina, threatening vision. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why does peripheral neuropathy increase the risk of foot ulcers in diabetic patients?

options.A: Nerve damage directly causes the skin to dissolve overnight
options.B: It completely stops blood flow to the lower extremities
options.C: Loss of protective sensation prevents patients from noticing minor injuries
options.D: It forces patients to walk with an abnormal posture

explanation: When sensation is lost, patients may step on sharp objects or develop blisters without feeling pain, leading to unnoticed wounds. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h8)
